request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).
request.prompt:

DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export pools as CSV" button (`data-testid="export-pools"`) to the Pools section, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

- **What it does:** it downloads `pools-<sheet>.csv`. The first line is `pool,member,share,cut`, then one line per member, with pools and members in the order they were added.
- **Where the values come from:** the export reads the same rows the pools list shows on screen. So a pool member is written as `pool:<name>`, the share is as entered, and the cut is exactly what the row shows: blank when there is none, and it follows changes such as a member retiring.
- **CSV quoting:** a field containing a quote, comma or line break is put in quotes, with any quotes inside doubled (e.g. `"Lee, Jo"`). Every line ends with a line feed.

The only file changed is `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/pools/pools.ts`; no server or stored-data changes were needed.

I copied the people export's small CSV-writing routine into the pools screen instead of moving it into a shared helper, to avoid touching the people screen. Moving it into one shared helper would be a small follow-up if you'd prefer the two exports use the same code.
